$comment: CONTRACT EXTENSION for demo-editing.html, layered on top of assets/demo/layers.json (which stays the canonical map/server contract — this file never overrides it). Server side this page reads the synthetic inspection layer on demo.honua.io, discovered in GET /odata/Layers by the first name in odata.layerNames that is published. The 2026-06-12 seed is service 'maui-inspections' (OData layer id 12, typed table public.maui_inspections with CHECK constraints mirroring 'categories'/'statuses'/'noteMaxLength' below). WRITE LANE: the page never ships a credential. When the data lane is live, Save sends the real anonymous OData PATCH and Add the POST; the server's answer decides (2xx live and re-read, 401/403 access policy, 402 license, 405/501 the layer does not accept writes, network unreachable). Writes are governed by the layer's access policy; capabilities.manifestPath is read only as an informational hint because the manifest reports every anonymous caller as insufficient-policy for edit.features.

odata.$layerNamesComment: OData layer names in preference order. maui-inspections is the 2026-06-12 seed, published storageMode=source over the typed table, so honua-server answers OData writes on it with 501 ProviderWriteNotSupported. maui-inspections-scratch is the managed-store editable copy described in honua-demo-infra runbook/editing-scratch-layer-anonymous-writes.md; the page prefers it when published.
odata.$etagComment: OData responses support optimistic concurrency via @odata.etag / If-Match (412 on mismatch), but the CORS preflight allow-headers list on demo.honua.io omits If-Match (re-checked 2026-10-24), so this page does not send it; PATCH without If-Match is last-write-wins, which is acceptable for a synthetic sandbox. The single-entity GET answers 200 again (2026-10-24) and is used to re-read a feature after a successful write.

geoservices.$comment: The same layer on the GeoServices surface — documented alternative read path. Esri FeatureServer applyEdits (the Pro editing surface) is deliberately NOT used by this page; open-protocol OData CRUD is the story.

map.$comment: Framed on Maui island — the inspection points span Kapalua to Hāna.
